statements.worth_reason: NVIDIA taking credit-support and revenue-share positions in cloud partners' capacity is a new binding obligation that changes its cash and credit risk and its revenue mix (the standard's own core example of a backstop plan announced without an amount).
A named early participant sizing its deployment under the new programme (up to 40,000 GB300) is demand evidence and the first size marker for NVIDIA's credit-support exposure.
statements.one_line_problem: Lost condition: the article presents Sharon AI as an early participant in NVIDIA's revenue-sharing/credit-support programme ('Early participants illustrate the scale of the initiative'); read alone, the record is a generic deployment plan and cannot be filed as evidence of NVIDIA's obligation.
statements.tier_note: party_statement (Sharon AI's announced plan, reported as such); nothing in the article calls it unconfirmed or credits an unnamed source, so rumour is wrong.

statements.worth_reason: A second named participant campus (about 170,000 GPUs, 360 MW) sizes the programme's potential scale and NVIDIA's credit exposure.
statements.one_line_problem: Lost condition: drops that Firmus is an early participant in NVIDIA's credit-support programme, which is why it matters to NVIDIA; also does not say the GPUs are NVIDIA's.
statements.tier_note: party_statement (Firmus's announced project, reported as such), not rumour.

missing_questions.what: Class C binding_obligation on NVDA: what amount of credit-support / revenue-backstop commitments to AI cloud partners will NVIDIA report in its FY2027 annual report (settled by the 10-K commitments and guarantees note). It passes the section 4 tests: it changes NVIDIA's cash and credit risk, it is checkable at a dated filing, and it is the article's main event; section 9.2 names this AI Compute Partnership obligation question as the one that must be opened.

grade_reason: The announcement itself is recorded correctly, but the binding-obligation question that this exact announcement should open is missing, and both participant records are tiered as rumours and lose their link to NVIDIA's programme.
standard_doubt: Tier table row 5 ('以上都不是、又没有出处的说法 → 传闻') turns an ordinary reported company plan ('Sharon AI plans to deploy up to 40,000 Grace Blackwell GB300 GPUs') into a rumour just because the reporter cites no source; an analyst reads it as the company's announced plan (party_statement). Row 2 covers 'announcements' but not plans, so the gap pushes routine reporting to the bottom tier.
